criterion: A launch against a gateway that rejects the key fails within about 3 seconds, whichever model is named or none.
evidence: cli test TestAGatewayThatRejectsTheKeyRefusesTheLaunchBeforeAnyAdapter: the named-model and no-model launches both refuse at the pre-flight, adapter-start is never invoked, the launch machinery runs 0.06s in-test; the built core runs 0.87s end to end with one instantly-refused probe. The probe is doctor's own request (ProbeListing, connect-timeout 2s, max-time 5s), the request the issue measured answering 401 in ~2.2s. The sandbox denies egress to a live 401 endpoint, so the live 401 itself was not re-timed here; the wait that made 7-92s was the adapter spin, which never starts now.

criterion: The first line of the failure says the key was rejected (HTTP 401) and names the command that replaces it.
evidence: Same test asserts the failure's one line carries 'rejected the API key', 'HTTP 401' and 'ccmorph config gw374': listingFailure prints '<endpoint> rejected the API key for 'gw374' (HTTP 401) — replace it with: ccmorph config gw374' as the launch's first and only failure line.

criterion: The launch failure and ccmorph doctor name the same fix command for the same rejection.
evidence: listingFailure (cli/models.go:106), the adapter's EXIT line (adapter/adapter.go) and doctor's gateway 401 row (util/doctor.go:168) all name 'ccmorph config <name>'; both probes are the same headerless request, so they detect the same rejection. The glue that pointed at 'ccmorph doctor' after a refusal is gone for refusals (TestAnAdapterRefusalStandsAlone), and TestARefusedListingNamesItsTrueCause pins the EXIT wording on both the named-model and no-model paths.

criterion: The screen does not mention an adapter for a profile that doctor says needs none.
evidence: Same cli test asserts the failure text never contains 'adapter': the refusal returns before adapterStart, so the 'Starting adapter' and waiting lines (which live inside util adapter-start, never invoked — asserted via the core-calls log) cannot print.

criterion: The gateway's log shows at most a few requests with the rejected key per launch.
evidence: Same test counts the pre-flight probe: exactly 1 listing request per launch, whichever shape; a 2xx answer is memoized into the pass's listing cache so the later l.listing reuses it — one request per route on the happy path too. Adapter-side, TestARefusedListingNamesItsTrueCause/a_model_is_named counts 0 inference requests on a refused listing, where the issue's log showed ~2.5 requests/s for 45-90s.
